findings.assessment: Baseline Evidence is strict and provider-neutral, carrying provider/profile, subject digest, raw/normalized results, confidence, limitations, locations and evidence links. A cross-provider behavioral graph linking static facts, runtime, memory, state and candidates is not demonstrated. Draft PR #29 adds a graph foundation but no static/runtime integrations; its tests were not executed. Further source review found existing specialized native and JavaScript application graphs and an EvidenceLedger. Preserve those graph details and use the ledger as the Evidence source of truth; the missing capability is the cross-domain projection joining them by provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Import static and runtime evidence for the same exact binary into one versioned graph.
Preserve provider identity, evidence IDs and raw provenance.
Keep conflicts and ambiguous address/function matches unresolved.
Test idempotent import, binary-hash isolation, migration and tamper rejection.

findings.assessment: Current maintenance scans caller-supplied captured bytes and explicitly disclaims live addresses and semantic fields. Draft PR #30 adds bounded offline allocation/write/free modeling, not live instrumentation or complete semantic heap recovery; tests not executed.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded typed trace ingestion with sequence/drop/truncation markers.
Test allocation reuse, lifetime, write bounds, use-after-free and alias ambiguity.
Compare semantic state across original/candidate runs; missing events remain INCOMPLETE.

findings.assessment: A durable bounded controller exists with binary identity, checkpoints, owned-process evidence and declared scenario comparison. Documented parity is limited to declared fixtures and narrow Calculator UI outputs. Draft PR #31 adds a pure byte minimizer; process execution, provenance binding, grammar generation and persistent corpus are explicitly absent; tests not executed.
acceptance_criteria: Bind comparisons to exact original/candidate hashes, environment, rules and raw captures.
Find/minimize mismatches under budgets; persist replayable regression inputs.
Test wrong identity, timeout, cancellation, nondeterminism, restart and interrupted resume.

findings.assessment: Baseline has narrow affine Z3 obligations under assumptions. Draft PR #32 adds QF_BV affine wraparound obligations, not general machine-code semantics or executable witness replay; tests not executed.
acceptance_criteria: Persist query hash, solver/version, binary/function mapping and assumptions.
Replay SAT witnesses against exact original/candidate binaries.
Report VERIFIED UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS, COUNTEREXAMPLE, UNKNOWN, TIMEOUT or UNSUPPORTED.

findings.assessment: Broad static-provider adapters and verification scripts exist; extend them instead of adding a second engine. Claims must remain tied to executed provider/version, target hash, profile and limitations. Not executed in this cloud shell.

Controlled process capture and Frida/LLDB paths exist. Documentation says ownership and output/time bounds are not an OS security sandbox. GUI/audio/GPU/native-Windows claims need separately evidenced platform workers.

No complete document-reader or media-player repair was found. GConv/QVM is real but partial: local 2003 Windows binaries have hashes, 120-script error parity is documented, but full VM/ABI work is unverified, source/build are not reverified in the case study, and target screenshots are absent. Calculator/arithmetic fixtures are narrow validations, not full maintenance cases. Draft PR #33 says no complete real legacy port is verified and presents an XMMS candidate, not an executed repair.

Maintenance intake validates caller-attested authorization and prepares skills/plans; it does not independently verify legal authority or autonomously repair arbitrary programs. Controller handles bounded caller-supplied plans and checkpoints, not a universal reverse-engineering loop.
PR #23 merged three skills and catalog contract coverage; #24 merged focused workflow validation. CI still needs an actual passing run for the path. Current head query did not establish one.
Baseline README is 44 KB and docs extensive. Draft PR #33 shortens/restructures README and adds case-study gates, but is documentation-only and states local build/lint were not executed.

MIT license, lawful-use policy and third-party inventory exist. Target authority is caller-attested, not independently verified. Original binaries/assets require separate provenance and redistribution review.

The repository already has typed native investigation relationships, a JavaScript application graph Evidence adapter, and an immutable Evidence ledger. A unified behavioral model must compose these systems and retain their detailed outputs rather than replacing or duplicating them.
acceptance_criteria: Existing native and JavaScript graph tests continue to pass.
Unified graph edges point to Evidence IDs held by the existing ledger/checkpoint.
Provider-specific graph payloads remain available through their original workflows.
